add.issue.name: A git user.email that is not an address blocks every board write

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing branch `Z0X5H17-link-email` at `81588492` (local-only, worktree `.claude/worktrees/Z0X5H17-link-email`).

`ensureEmailLinked` (`source/lib/board/board-contributor.ts:69`) is the only one of the three writers that never calls `isValidEmail`. The MCP door checks it (`emails.ts:47`), the materializer checks it (`board-materialize.ts:690`), the unattended write path does not.

Git accepts any string in `user.email`. `readGitEmail` normalizes and stores it. Then on every write: the hook writes `link.contributor.email`, the materializer rejects it with `materializeSkip`, `materializeAndPersist` returns that failure **without persisting** (`event-write.ts:50-53`), `ensureEmailLinked` turns it into `failed()`, and `beforeWrite` propagates it — aborting the user's own write. Nothing is recorded to stop it, so every subsequent write fails the same way, on the TUI, the GUI and the MCP alike.

Reproduced at that SHA with three realistic values — `Jonatan Lampa <jola@x.com>` (a pasted whole ident), `root`, `a@b@c`. Renaming a ticket fails with:

```
link contributor email failed, not an email address: jonatan lampa <jola@x.com>
```

**Fix:** bail with `succeeded()`, not `failed()`, when the configured address fails `isValidEmail` — the same shape as the existing "not when the repository has no configured address" branch.

**Fold in with the fix:** `writer()` in `auto-link-email.test.ts` returns `succeeded` unconditionally, so the test double is more permissive than the real write path and cannot catch this class of bug. Pointing its `writeOne` at the real `materialize()` turns this red.

add.issue.name: The Stats tab counts raw git names, so one person reads as two authors

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing branch `Z0X5H17-link-email` at `81588492`.

`withCommitAuthors` is applied on the scrubber's window (`websocket.ts:265`) and on a ticket's Code tab (`websocket.ts:343`), but not on the stats path. `epiq-issue-stats.ts:63` keeps `commit.author` raw, and `change-shape.ts:46` then deduplicates authors by that raw string and shows the count.

So one person committing from two linked addresses reads as one person on the Code tab and as **"2 Authors"** on the Stats tab — the same split `bdeaf8fb` closed between the scrubber and the log, in the one place where the number is the whole point.

Fixing it means deciding whether `StatsCommit` should carry the resolved identity, which makes it part of the stats cache key — see `RP9A3HF`.

add.issue.name: The identity panel reports unrelated socket failures as its own

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing branch `Z0X5H17-link-email` at `81588492`.

`App.tsx:879` calls `contributorEmails.onMessage(message)` on every socket message, and `use-contributor-emails.ts` treats any `{type: 'failed'}` as an email failure: it sets `lastAction` to that message and clears `loading`.

There are four such senders in `websocket.ts` (151, 506, 665, 848), and the one at 665 is a **broadcast**, so it reaches every client. While the panel is open, an unrelated failure — another action's write, or "Read-only while viewing history" from somewhere else — is shown in red under "Claim an address" as though the link had failed.

The handler needs to scope itself to its own round trip rather than to the message type alone. Note that `emails:get`, `email:link` and `email:unlink` are the only handlers here that send no `requestId`, which is what a scoped reply would need.

add.issue.name: Two dead exports from the email-link work, and a git-email cache nothing clears

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing branch `Z0X5H17-link-email` at `81588492`. Tidy-up, not a bug.

- `resolveEmailOwner` (`source/lib/model/email-link.ts`) has no production caller; only its own test exercises it. `emailOwnerIndex` is what the code actually uses.
- `forgetGitEmail` (`source/lib/config/git-identity.ts`) has no caller at all, including tests — although its docstring says it exists for tests.

The second one matters slightly more than dead code usually does: `readGitEmail` caches per repository root and nothing ever invalidates it, so in a long-running GUI server a `git config user.email` change needs a restart to be noticed. Either wire `forgetGitEmail` into whatever should clear it, or drop it and say in `readGitEmail` that the value is fixed for the life of the process.

add.issue.comment.md:
Reviewed this as part of the branch review (`81588492`). The shape holds up — every predicate reads only the ordered log, so two replicas cannot disagree, and the author-or-target removal rule is the right narrow half.

One residual I'd put on the ticket rather than leave in `canRemoveEmailLink`'s docstring, because it is an accepted consequence rather than an implementation detail: **a first claimant permanently denies the true owner, with no recourse at all.** The auto-link goes silent on a claimed address, a manual claim only makes it contested so it resolves to neither, and the owner cannot strip the other claim. The panel diagnoses it well ("Already claimed by X… Your commits show as theirs") but there is no cure short of signed commits.

It is reachable without an attacker — two colleagues sharing a `user.email`, or one honest mistake — and it is permanent and replicated. Worth stating as decided, so it reads as a known cost rather than something discovered later.

add.issue.name: A failed candidate scan is indistinguishable from having nothing to claim

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing branch `Z0X5H17-link-email` at `8e95265f`, on the new `findEmailCandidates`.

`findEmailCandidates` (`source/lib/repository/email-candidates.ts:42`) returns `[]` whenever git exits non-zero. The panel renders that as **"Nothing left to claim here."** — the same thing it says on a repository where everything is genuinely claimed. Since claiming from the offered list is now the *only* way to link an address, a scan that fails silently means the feature is simply unavailable and nothing says why.

Two ways to reach it:

- `git log --branches` over all history is not in `SLOW_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS`, so it gets the 10s `GIT_TIMEOUT_MS`. A large enough repository times out, and the SIGTERM reads as "nothing to claim".
- The scan runs on every `emails:get` and again on every link and unlink (`websocket.ts:277` and `:294` each await it alongside the list), with no cache — so opening the panel and claiming three addresses is seven full-history walks.

Worth returning a `Result` and letting the panel say "couldn't read this repository's history" instead of an empty list. Caching per repo root, as `readGitEmail` now does with a TTL, would also make the panel's own round trips cheap.

Separately and more minor: `--branches` covers local branches only, so on a fresh clone with just `main` checked out, an address that only appears on an unfetched branch is never offered. Probably right — your own commits are usually local — but it is a choice worth stating rather than leaving implied.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: fixed at `abf6d0db`. The stats cache key is now `[repoRoot, ref, sha:author...]`, so the resolved author is part of what the entry is keyed on and a link that changes who a commit belongs to is a different key.

Keyed on the resolved names rather than on the link log, which is the better of the two: a link touching none of a ticket's commits evicts nothing. The comment above the key was updated to stay true, which is what made it wrong the first time.

Verified independently: I reverted the key to its old sha-only form at that SHA and the new `re-derives after a link changes who a commit resolves to` test goes red; restored, it passes. So the regression is genuinely pinned, not just described.
add.issue.comment.author: YEZWEN8801VDBA4Q79PDYKGCPX

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: both halves fixed at `abf6d0db`.

`findEmailCandidates` returns a `Result`, and a non-zero git exit becomes `Could not read this repository's history: <stderr>` rather than an empty list — so a failed scan no longer reads as a history with nothing left in it. The panel renders it in red instead of as the empty state.

The walk is cached per repository for 15s, and the cache holds only the raw git output: the claimed-address filtering runs fresh over it, so a link still changes the offered list immediately while opening the panel and claiming three addresses is one walk rather than seven. That split is the right one — it was the walk that was expensive, not the filtering.

The `--branches` note in the description was left as-is, which I think is correct: your own commits are local, and widening it to remotes would offer colleagues' addresses from branches you have never worked on.
add.issue.comment.author: YEZWEN8801VDBA4Q79PDYKGCPX

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: closed out at `abf6d0db`. `resolveEmailOwner` is deleted and its tests now go through `emailOwnerIndex` — the same index production matches commits with, so the tests exercise the real path rather than a parallel one that only they used.

That is the better reading of the finding. "Test-only" was the more accurate description than "dead": a helper nothing ships but the tests trust is worse than an unused one, because it can drift from the code it stands in for without a single test going red.

With the 30s TTL on `readGitEmail` from `8e95265f`, both halves of this ticket are done.

add.issue.name: The TUI passes a git address where a git name belongs, so it ranks your own old addresses last

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing branch `Z0X5H17-link-email` at `b25c74b5`.

`findEmailCandidates` takes `names`, documented as "Whatever the asker is called: their board name, their git name". The two call sites disagree:

- `suggestOwnEmails` (`emails.ts:240`) → `[userName, await readGitName(repoRoot)]` — correct
- `setEmailsCommand` (`set-emails.cmd.ts:68`) → `[userName, gitEmail]` — the address, not the name

`words()` then tokenizes the address, so the identity tokens for the TUI become `jola`, `example`, `com` instead of `jola`, `jonatan`, `lampa`.

**Proved** against the history `source/scripts/scratch-board.mjs` builds — board name `jola`, git `Jonatan Lampa <jola@example.com>`, plus `J. Lampa <j.lampa@oldjob.com>` and `Sam Rivers <sam@example.com>`:

| `names` passed | `jola@example.com` | `j.lampa@oldjob.com` | `sam@example.com` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[board, gitEmail]` (today) | yes | **no** | no |
| `[board, gitName]` (documented) | yes | **yes** | no |

The old-job address is the one the scratch script's own comment calls "the case the feature exists for" — it matches nothing you are called now, and the git name is what would have caught it.

**Impact is ordering, not filtering.** `EmailCandidates.tsx` does not read `looksLikeYours`, and `setEmailsCommand` offers every candidate, so nothing is hidden — but `findEmailCandidates` sorts `looksLikeYours` first, so in the TUI your own old address sinks below a colleague's with more commits. The spurious `example` and `com` tokens can also promote an unrelated address whose local part or author name contains one of them as a whole word.

The sharper problem is the disagreement. `email-candidates.ts` opens by saying it is shared "because the TUI's setup step and the MCP tool have to offer the same list — two scanners would mean two answers to 'which of these are mine', and the one the user was shown would depend on where they happened to be standing." That is exactly what one scanner fed two different inputs produces.

Fix is one argument: pass `readGitName(repoRoot)`. Worth a test pinning the two call sites to the same tokens, since nothing currently fails when they drift.

add.issue.comment.md:
claude/oskar, reviewing `b25c74b5`. A process note rather than a defect.

This ticket carries a `Solution:` comment saying the MCP half is done and the remaining work is "a prefilled default in `:config username`". Eleven commits have since landed under this ref, and they are a good deal more than that:

- a command-line auto-complete and validation framework (`command-validation.ts` +158, `command-auto-complete*`, plus `command-auto-complete.test.ts`)
- a TUI identity screen (`IdentityUI.tsx` +188, `EmailCandidates.tsx` +113, `email-offers.state.ts`)
- a new `:emails-unclaim` command (`unclaim-email.cmd.ts` +70)
- `npm run start:scratch-board`, a throwaway repo and unconfigured machine for walking setup (+88)
- board-attribution changes in `timeline-index.ts` and `epiq-time-travel.ts`

43 files and ~1700 insertions against a description about seeding one field from git.

Each of the first four stands on its own — someone could pick up "auto-complete for command arguments" or "a scratch board for walking setup" cold, and neither needs this ticket's context. The commit↔ticket linking is what suffers: this ticket's commit list no longer tells the story its description and `Solution:` comment tell, and the auto-complete work is now findable only by knowing it happened to ride along with a username default.

Not asking for a rewrite of landed history — the refs are consistent and that is what matters most. Worth either widening the description to say what this ticket actually became, or splitting the follow-on work onto its own tickets before merge so the board keeps its traceability.

The work itself reviews well; see `2YGHD6Z` for the one defect I found.

add.issue.name: readGitName is uncached on the per-request boot path, at ~87ms a call

edit.description.md:
Found reviewing branch `Z0X5H17-link-email` at `fbaea9ac`.

The fix for `2YGHD6Z` added `gitName` to the settings store, filled in `boot.ts:156`:

```ts
patchSettingsState({
  gitEmail: await readGitEmail(repoRootResult.value),
  gitName: await readGitName(repoRootResult.value),
});
```

`readGitEmail` is served from a 30s cache. `readGitName`, in the same file, has none — it spawns `git config --get user.name` on every call.

That line sits **above** the fast-path skip at `boot.ts:173`, and `boot()` runs on every MCP call and every websocket message. The comment inside `readGitEmail` says exactly why that matters: *"`boot()` runs on every MCP call and every socket message, above the fast path that exists to avoid redundant work, so an uncached read here would spawn a git process per request to answer the same thing every time."* The name read now does what the address read was cached to stop doing.

**Measured** at that SHA, 200 calls of each after warm-up:

| | total | per call |
|---|---|---|
| `readGitEmail` (cached) | 0.1ms | 0.001ms |
| `readGitName` (uncached) | 17,333.9ms | **86.7ms** |

87ms is inflated — this machine had several sessions running — but the shape is not load-dependent: one is a map lookup and the other is a subprocess, and it is paid per request on every surface.

Fix is to give `readGitName` the same `Cached`/`CACHE_MS` treatment `readGitEmail` already has, ideally by folding both into one cached read of the pair, since they are always wanted together and come from the same config.

Minor, same area: `suggestOwnEmails` (`emails.ts:240`) still calls `await readGitName(repoRoot)` directly rather than reading the settings store the three TUI call sites now use. Less hot, but it is the same value read two ways.

add.issue.comment.md:
Verified at `fbaea9ac`. All three call sites pass `gitName`, and the behavioural test genuinely bites — I restored `gitEmail` at all three and `knows an old address of yours by the name on its commits` goes red, green again with `gitName`. Right call making it behavioural rather than an argument assertion.

One correction to the comment above, which is why `C8D4EJM` is now open: it is **not** true that there is no extra git call. `boot.ts:156` fills `gitName` with `readGitName`, which has no cache, while `readGitEmail` beside it has a 30s one — and that line sits above the fast-path skip, so every MCP call and every socket message spawns a `git config --get user.name`. Measured 86.7ms a call against 0.001ms for the cached address read.

The fix here is right; the settings store just is not yet the cheap read the comment assumes.

add.issue.name: Other repos: a fetch deletes the shared clone when project.json stops listing the repo

edit.description.md:
From the review of 4SC2RXY (Commits from other repos), branch `4SC2RXY-multi-repo-commits`. Fix before merge.

After every fetch, `fetchAll` re-reads `project.json` and deletes the clone of any repo no longer listed (`commit-repo-fetch.ts:722-728`). A branch switch, pull or rebase in the worktree during a fetch is enough: the clone and its status are gone, for every worktree sharing it. Reproduced: `project.json` rewritten without `repos` mid-fetch → outcome "Fetched", clones dir empty.

Contradicts PRZTPYJ call 4 and the module's own comment at `:580-583` (only an explicit remove deletes a clone).

Fix: `removeRepo` leaves a marker (or an in-process pending-removal set) and the cleanup acts only on that.

add.issue.name: Other repos: a failed fetch is not usefully reported — the GUI shows the git command line, and nothing after a sync

edit.description.md:
From the review of 4SC2RXY (Commits from other repos), branch `4SC2RXY-multi-repo-commits`. Fix before merge: "a repo that fails to fetch is reported" is a requirement.

- The panel shows `repo.error.split('\n')[0]` (`ManageReposModal.tsx:36`). An `execGit` failure's first line is always `git <argv>`, so the user reads `git -c core.hooksPath=… clone --bare …` and never "repository not found" / "authentication failed". Seen in a scratch GUI.
- The same string goes to `epiq_sync` / `epiq_repo_list`: ~500 chars of flags and home-directory paths before the reason, and the 2000-char slice (`commit-repo-fetch.ts:545`) is spent on them first.
- After a GUI sync or autosync a failed fetch is not shown at all: `fetchReposAndBroadcast` (`websocket.ts:118`) broadcasts only when a repo changed. An open panel keeps "not fetched yet", the sync reads as success. The MCP door does append "could not fetch X".
- A clone whose log cannot be read (32MB cap, timeout) shows zero commits with only a log line (`commit-timeline.ts:224`).
- A registered repo with no commits yet fails every fetch on the `--deepen=1` step (`commit-repo-fetch.ts:262`).

Fix: keep git's stderr (last `fatal:` line) and drop the argv line in `fetchOne`; broadcast on a failed outcome too; put a read failure in the repo's state; skip the deepen on an empty clone.

add.issue.name: Other repos: several processes on one clone — an explicit fetch answered ok without fetching, an orphaned git's locks cleared, GUI not told

edit.description.md:
From the review of 4SC2RXY (Commits from other repos), branch `4SC2RXY-multi-repo-commits`. All in `commit-repo-fetch.ts`; the first two reproduced with separate processes on a scratch global dir.

1. **Explicit fetch answered ok, nothing fetched.** The throttle check runs under the clone lock, after a git spawn (`:511-535`), so every autosync tick in every process holds the lock briefly. An explicit fetch arriving then gets `ok: true, "Another process is fetching it"` (`:503`), the other process answers "Fetched recently", and the clone stays behind. The GUI says "Fetched 1 repo". Fix: decide the throttle before taking the lock; an explicit caller retries briefly and reports "skipped", not ok.
2. **A dead holder's lock is taken while its git child still runs.** Nothing kills the child when a TUI quits or a server is killed mid-fetch; the next process takes the lock at once, `clearStaleGitLocks` deletes the live child's lock files and a second fetch starts in the same clone. Same root: `sweepPending` deletes a `.pending` clone an orphaned `git clone` may still be writing; the timeout path releases the lock right after SIGTERM, before `close`. Fix: kill clone-git children on exit, wait for `close` after a timeout kill, record the child pid in the lock.
3. **GUI clients are not told when another process moved the clone.** `changed` compares refs around this process's own fetch only, so after an agent's `epiq_sync` fetched, the GUI server's pass finds nothing new and sends no `repos:changed`. Fix: a per-process last-seen ref signature per clone, compared on every pass.
4. Any failure of `git config --get remote.origin.url` (a timeout under load) deletes the whole clone (`:448-455`, `:511-515`). Delete only when the read succeeded and names another repo.
5. Plausible: `git maintenance run --auto` after each fetch can detach and hold `packed-refs.lock` past epiq's lock. Add `gc.auto=0` / `maintenance.auto=false` to the clone flags.

add.issue.name: Code repos in the GUI: a hidden repo stays hidden with no control, "fetching…" latches, and smaller panel gaps

edit.description.md:
From the review of 4SC2RXY (Commits from other repos), branch `4SC2RXY-multi-repo-commits`.

1. **Hidden repo with no way back.** Untick "this repo", then move to a window (or remove the other repo) where only one repo has commits: the toggle group is not drawn (`ScrubberSelects.tsx:525`, `repos.length > 1`) but `withoutHiddenRepos` still drops every commit. No code on the chart or log until reload. Fix in `commit-repo-filter.ts`: ignore hidden keys not among the current ones. Fix before merge.
2. **`fetching` latches.** "fetch now" on a long first clone, then the socket drops: the reply goes only to the old socket, so the button stays "fetching…" and disabled for the life of the page (`use-repos.ts`). Clear on reconnect or on open.
3. Leaving the date field without changing it sends `repo:add`: `project.json` is rewritten, the timeline cache cleared and `repos:changed` broadcast to every client (`ManageReposModal.tsx:89`). Upsert should report "unchanged" and skip both.
4. The URL input is cleared before the reply, so a refused URL loses what was typed (`ManageReposModal.tsx:112`). Clear on an ok reply.
5. Escape works only once focus is inside the modal; no `role="dialog"`, no accessible names on the input and selects. It is the fifth copy of the backdrop/frame literals — a shared modal shell would own dismissal and focus.
6. The filter's state, two memos and a toggle sit in `App.tsx` and are passed down three levels; a `useCommitRepoFilter` hook in `commit-repo-filter.ts` is where item 1's fix belongs too.

add.issue.name: Other repos: reading gaps — clone logs re-read every 5s, order across repos, a fork's squashed share, uncapped TUI patch, 21st repo

edit.description.md:
From the review of 4SC2RXY (Commits from other repos), branch `4SC2RXY-multi-repo-commits`.

1. **Clone logs are cached 5s like the board's own, and a failed read not at all** (`commit-timeline.ts:155`, `:195`). Only a fetch changes a clone, yet a `since: all` repo pays a full `git log --shortstat` whenever the cache lapses, serially ahead of the board's own commits; one past the 32MB cap is re-read until killed on every call. Cache clone reads, failures included, until `invalidateCommitTimelineCache`.
2. **Newest-first breaks across repos.** `mergeNewestFirst` compares list heads only, so a rebased commit with an old author date holds back every newer one behind it (`commit-timeline.ts:257`). Reproduced. Reaches the TUI Diff list, which 200 commits stats keep, and which repo leads the squashed diff. The GUI re-sorts and is unaffected.
3. **A fork's squashed share counts the ticket's own commit as foreign.** `squashInRepo` decides ownership from the deduplicated list (`commit-diff.ts:581`), so a shared commit listed under the first source makes the fork's range non-contiguous and its lines appear in both. Reproduced. Pass each source's pre-dedup matches.
4. **The TUI patch of a clone commit is capped only at 256MB** (`commit-diff.ts:53`). A 40MB file gave 1.5M rows and 514MB RSS. The GUI path is capped at 8MB. Same for stats, whose 64MB check runs after the batch has buffered (`patch-scan.ts:372`). Pass a small `maxOutput`.
5. **The 20-repo cap is applied on read only.** A 21st repo is written and answered "Added", then never listed or fetched (`commit-repos.ts:330` vs `:206`). Refuse it in `upsertCommitRepo`.
6. A subject holding `\x1e`/`\x1f` forges a log record: a fake sha and author on a ticket (`commit-timeline.ts:39`). Already true of the board's own repo; now reachable from repos the board owner does not control. Use `-z` and check the sha is 40 hex.
7. Stats fail whole when one clone's `git show` fails (`patch-scan.ts:389`); the timeline and squashed diff skip the clone.

add.issue.name: Sync lock: a lock that vanishes mid-acquire is broken as stale, so two processes can both hold it

edit.description.md:
Found while reviewing 4SC2RXY (Commits from other repos), which reuses this lock for clones. Already on `main`: it guards the board's own sync.

In `acquireLockFile` (`source/git/sync-lock.ts`): the `link` fails because A holds the lock; A releases; `readHolder` finds nothing and returns null; `claimOver(null)` is `stale`; `rmSync(lockPath)` then removes whatever is there now — a third process's fresh lock — and this process writes its own. Two processes judging the same dead holder do the same to each other.

A stress of 8 processes looping acquire/release: 1,345 acquisitions, 413 overlapping another holder. Real odds per sync are low, but many sessions autosync one board here.

Fix: on a missing lock, retry the `link` rather than breaking; break by renaming to a unique name and checking its content before removing.

add.issue.comment.md:
From the review of 4SC2RXY (Commits from other repos):

- The description's fourth item looks done already: the window now drops by commit date (`commit-timeline.ts`, `%ct` against `notBefore`), matching the clone's cut. No test pins it (DKM832Q).
- `removeRepoClone` checks the clone name's basename, not the id: `../../x/app-0123456789ab` would pass and resolve outside the clones dir. Not reachable today — every caller passes a registered id. Test `${repoId}.git` itself.
- `core.hooksPath=/dev/null/epiq-no-hooks` is a creatable path on Windows (`<drive>:\dev\null\…`). Point it at an empty directory epiq owns.
- `followDefaultBranch` writes the remote's branch name into HEAD and the refspec unchecked; a server advertising `refs/heads/*` widens `default` to all. It also only follows a rename: a default switched to another existing branch keeps reading the old one.
- git's wording is matched in English (`couldn't find remote ref`, `no commits selected…`); a localized git skips both recoveries. Set `LC_ALL=C` for clone git.
- The clone flags are listed twice (`HERMETIC` and `cloneDirArgs`) and reach git doubled; one list should own them.
- `epiq_repo_remove` refuses a label that `:config repoRemove` takes; the TUI command restates the id/URL match and the add/remove sequences from `mcp/api/repos.ts`. `cwdByRepo` is built identically in `issue-stats.ts` and `commit-diff.ts`.
- Tool text: `epiq_sync` still says pull and push only; `epiq_repo_add` says "remote URL" while `file:///` passes.
- Labels are lowercased and cut at 24 chars with no ellipsis in the panel.
- Comments: the clone-args doc block in `git-utils.ts` sits on `STABLE_OUTPUT`, 30 lines above what it describes; "runs exactly as it always has" is history; several run to a paragraph.
